newsitem.title: USA: Group sues Riverside, Calif., over lighting tax.
newsitem.headline: Group sues Riverside, Calif., over lighting tax.

text.p: A prominent taxpayers group on Wednesday sued the city of Riverside, alleging its lighting assessment violated California's Proposition 218.
The Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association asked Riverside's Superior Court to revoke the tax, which was recently approved by 50.5 percent of local voters.

The association contends that Riverside's assessment failed to meet the state's strict two-thirds vote requirement for special taxes and violated provisions of Proposition 218, the so-called Right to Vote on Taxes Act.
The proposition has made it more difficult for local governments across the state to raise taxes.
The Riverside lawsuit was the second filed by the association over Proposition 218, which was approved by state voters last November. The association sued San Diego in June.
Jonathan Coupal, the association's director of legal affairs, said he planned to file several similar lawsuit against other local governments in the coming months.
"We are now lining them up and trying to pick them off one at a time," Coupal said.
